description: Interpolates the HARMONIC PARTIALS of pitched source 1 towards those of pitched source 2 - a pitched-sound-specific crossover, distinct from newmorph (which moves spectral peaks) and morph (whole-spectrum). Source-verified engine: the output is built window-by-window on INFILE2's frames and timeline - each output window keeps infile2's partial frequencies, every NON-harmonic channel is ZEROED, and each harmonic's amplitude is interpolated from infile2's level toward infile1's harmonic-amplitude profile by 'interp' (0 = infile2's own harmonic levels, 1 = infile1's colouration fully imposed). DURATION RULE (verified both orders via pvoc synth round-trips): output = infile2's duration, always - (2.0, 1.5) pair -> 1.5122, (1.5, 2.0) -> 2.0114, (3.0, 1.5) -> 1.5122 (within ~1 analysis window of indur2; infile1's length never matters). Before interpolating, the program pitch-tracks both files and finds infile1's ATTACK (loudest harmonic-energy window); windows after the attack are mapped by the ratio of the two files' tail lengths. Deterministic (byte-identical data chunks run to run). All 9 parameters are required positionals; only interp accepts a breakpoint file.
musical_use: Recolour one pitched sound with the harmonic colouration of another: because everything non-harmonic is zeroed and the frequencies stay infile2's, the render is a purified, harmonics-only version of sound 2 whose partial LEVELS lean toward sound 1 as interp rises - a formant-like colouration transfer between pitched sources (the manual likens results to GLISTEN; NEWMORPH is the peak-based alternative and usually the smoother morph). With a rising interp breakpoint (0 -> 1 over the file) sound 2 progressively takes on sound 1's harmonic balance as it plays. tuning widens the semitone tolerance for counting a partial as harmonic (forgiving values use more of the sound); thresh discards weak partials (high thresh + high interp leaves virtually only the colouration); level scales infile1's contribution. Works only on material the pitch-tracker can follow - use cleanly pitched sources with a clear attack near the start, and put the sound whose TIMELINE you want to keep in the infile2 slot (the output is always infile2's length).

tuning.description: Range in semitones within which partials count as 'in tune' with the harmonic series (CDP-enforced 0-6, refusal verbatim '(0.000000 to 6.000000)'; source default 1). Higher = more forgiving, more of sound 2 kept. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 ... brkpnt_files not permitted.').

minwin.description: Minimum number of adjacent pitched windows for a pitch value to register (source default 2). CDP-enforced 0 to an input-dependent window-count ceiling ('(0.000000 to 525.000000)' on the 2.0 s + 1.5 s probe pair). Scalar only (parameter 2).

signois.description: Signal-to-noise ratio in dB; windows further below the loudest are ignored by the pitch tracker (CDP-enforced 0-1000; source default 80). Scalar only (parameter 3).

harmcnt.description: How many of the 8 loudest spectral peaks must be harmonics to confirm the sound is pitched (CDP-enforced 1-8; source default 5). Scalar only (parameter 4).

lo.description: Lowest acceptable pitch (CDP-enforced 10 Hz to nyquist/8 - '(10.000000 to 2756.250000)' at 44.1 kHz, input-dependent ceiling). lo >= hi refused 'ERROR: Impossible pitch range specified.' Scalar only (parameter 5).

hi.description: Highest acceptable pitch (same CDP-enforced bounds as lo). Scalar only (parameter 6).

thresh.description: Minimum acceptable partial level, relative (CDP-enforced 0-1; source default 0.02). High values strip everything but the strongest partials. Scalar only (parameter 7).

level.description: Scales SOURCE 1's harmonic-level contribution before interpolation (source: src1level *= level; CDP-enforced 0-1, default 1). Scalar only (parameter 8).

interp.description: Degree of interpolation of the harmonic amplitudes from infile2's own levels (0) toward infile1's profile (1). The ONLY time-variable parameter (brk verified: 0->1 ramp differs from both scalar endpoints). CDP itself RESCALES the breakpoint's time axis to infile2's duration (source: ratio = duration2/lasttime); first time must be 0, times must advance, values 0-1, ';' comments allowed; a single-pair file collapses to a scalar.

examples.description: Full harmonic recolouring: sound 2 purified to its partials, levels drawn to sound 1's balance.
examples.expected_use: Output = infile2's duration; non-harmonic material removed, harmonic amplitudes follow infile1.

examples.description: Progressive takeover - interp as a rising breakpoint (e.g. '0 0 / 2 1').
examples.expected_use: Sound 2 starts as its own harmonics-only self and ends wearing sound 1's harmonic balance.

known_issues: DURATION: always infile2's duration (verified (2.0,1.5)->1.5122, (1.5,2.0)->2.0114, (3.0,1.5)->1.5122 via pvoc synth round-trips; ~1 window short). Put the timeline-owner second. Multi-input entry - the duration pre-flight uses indur2.

ATTACK GATE (content refusal): infile1's attack (loudest harmonic-energy window) must fall before the END of infile2 - verbatim 'ERROR: Attack time on 1st source is at or beyond end of 2nd.' A slow-swelling infile1 whose peak lands late also triggers 'WARNING: Attack time of 1st sound not close to start of sound'. Use sources with an attack near the start.

Output is HARMONICS-ONLY: every channel not matching a harmonic of infile2's tracked pitch is zeroed (source spec_interp), so even at interp 0 the render is a purified version of sound 2, not a pass-through.

UNDOCUMENTED FLAG -a (source vflag AMP_SCALING): shapes sound 2's level fluctuations under sound 1's gross envelope; accepted and output-changing (verified). A second declared flag -p is accepted but was a byte-identical no-op on the probes - left uncurated.

Parameters 1-8 all refuse breakpoint files ('Cannot read parameter N ... brkpnt_files not permitted.', N = 1-8, all probed); only interp (parameter 9) is time-variable, and CDP rescales its time axis to infile2's duration itself.
Floods stdout with one '0 min X.XX sec' progress print per window plus the family 'WARNING: failed to write PEAK data' - harmless, not errors.
Wav input refused ('File ... is not of correct type') - inputs must be .ana; the engine auto-PVOCs wav inputs.
Deterministic: repeat runs byte-identical in the data chunk (compare data chunks, not raw bytes - the .ana header DATE stamp differs).
